items.title: Phoebe Jacobs and Jackie Harris interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rome, New York, August 21, 2006
items.q: I’ve got to go back to Eubie. Because Eubie wrote a song during World War I... And he went to Paris with James Reese Europe in 1919 or 1920 I believe.

ctx.x: Did it surprise you that more of them did not turn out to be bitter with that kind of treatment?

Well again I’ve got to go back to Eubie. Because Eubie wrote a song during World War I, I don’t know if you’re aware about it, of the fact that the United States Army was segregated. And he went to Paris with James Reese Europe in 1919 or 1920 I believe. And he visited hospitals there and he watched a black soldier giving a blood transfusion to a white soldier. That’s when he was tempted to write this song which he wrote, called “We Are Americans Too” which was so illustrious of what people like Eubie felt. And…
Well said. Do you recall in the early — was it at the club that you were working at , was it called —
